newsitem.title: POLAND: FOCUS-Poland offers KGHM copper firm from June 30.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Poland offers KGHM copper firm from June 30.

text.p: Poland on June 30 launches its offer of up to 36 percent of copper producer KGHM Polska Miedz SA, whose initial valuation at between three and 4.6 billion zlotys makes it the country's biggest-ever privatisation.

KGHM's chief executive Stanislaw Siewierski told a news conference on Thursday that an initial price range for the public offer of up to 72 million out of KGHM's existing 200 million shares had been set at 15-23 zlotys per share.

"The price brackets have been set at between 15 and 23 zlotys...but the final price range might still be changed," Siewierski said after the Polish Securities Commission gave its go-ahead to the offer of KGHM, Poland's sole copper producer.
"This decision crowns several years of efforts by the company's management aimed at privatising the company," Siewierski said.
"We have decided that now is the right moment at which the company meets all the criteria to become a listed company."

The initial pricing makes the issue Poland's biggest privatisation to date. The Bank Handlowy offer now underway values the whole bank at 2.6-3.26 billion zlotys and the public offer at about one billion zlotys.

Poland is offering 55 million KGHM shares, or 27.5 percent of the total equity for public subscription between June 30 and July 4. Some 20 million shares are earmarked for domestic small and large investors and 35 million for foreign investors.

This may be increased by another 10 million shares if demand proves strong. The offering's global coordinators, United Bank of Switzerland, Barclays de Zoete Wedd and brokerage Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy will have an option to buy an additional seven million shares.
The privatisation plan also assumes that, up to 15 percent of KGHM would be set aside for about 50,000 present and former employees, leaving the state treasury with 49 percent.

Under the plan, the entire foreign tranche would be set aside for Global Depositary Receipts that would be issued by Citibank and Poland has earlier said it planned to list KGHM GDRs on the London stock exchange.
Siewierski said book building among domestic and foreign large investors would determine a minimum price for conclusive bids from large players, which will set the final strike price.
Shares in the domestic large investor tranche will be alloted at special bourse sessions from July 5-6 and in the domestic retail tranche at a special bourse session on July 7.
All shares in the foreign tranche are to be the basis for a Global Depositary Receipts (GDR) issue.
Siewierski said KGHM hoped to start trading on the Warsaw bourse by mid-July.
KGHM earned net 115.7 million zlotys on sales of 971 million in the first quarter of 1997 after posting a net profit of 147.2 million zlotys on sales of 3.35 billion in the whole of 1996.
